strings.patient_bundles.patient_sagiri_sakurai.p: Sagiri Sakurai
“Hospitalization? Well, now I really do need to take sick leave. Doctor, how many days are we looking at? I need to arrange the handover and leave paperwork right away.”
“All right. If something's wrong with my body, I can't just push through it. I'll leave work to my colleagues and put my treatment in your hands.”
“Wait, that isn't the procedure we just confirmed, is it? Even when I fly a test machine, I double-check the checklist. We can't skip that step in surgery.”
“Now that's clear. You handle the medical decisions, and I'll focus on cooperating—a clear division of responsibilities. I like it.”
“Just ‘follow the procedure’? I'm not fond of long reports either, but you could at least tell me what's coming next.”
“Don't worry. I've always been good at entrusting tasks to reliable people... That said, my heart's beating much faster than I expected.”
“General anesthesia... Handing over all control just like that really is a first for me. Please tell me how it went as soon as I wake up.”
“An epidural... I'll be awake, but I won't be able to move my lower body? Understanding it is one thing. I really don't relish experiencing it myself.”
“With local anesthesia, I can still talk to you, right? Good. If anything hurts in a way that feels wrong, I'll tell you immediately.”
“What? No anesthesia at all? I can pilot a test machine, but I've never trained to lie still while someone cuts me open! Doctor, are you serious?”
“All right, I'll stop putting on a brave face. I'll think of it as handing you the controls this time... When I wake up, just let me know everything went smoothly.”
“Wait! I said I'd cooperate, not that I wouldn't feel pain! Doctor, let me finish first...!”
“D-don't hold me down without warning! I know I need to stay still, but the scalpel is right here... At least tell me what you're doing next!”
“All right, I'll try not to move. It's just that being held steady like this makes it even clearer that I'm really on the operating table.”
“My legs are still there, but they don't feel like mine... I won't move around. Please let me know you're still beside me.”
“All right, I'm in your hands—w-wait! Don't bring that knife down... I-I'm really scared now!”
“...Have you started cutting already? There's no sharp pain, but it feels like something's being pushed apart inside... So it really has begun.”
“Hss...! The surface feels all right, but that tugging deeper inside just now felt awful... Doctor, I need to say something.”
“Aah—!! It hurts! It really hurts! W-wait... I can't take it! Doctor, please stop for a moment!”
“...Thank you. Let me catch my breath first. A moment ago, I thought I could handle this easily... Looks like I overestimated myself.”
“Don't move, right... I heard you. I'll try, but I really want to pull away right now. Please keep a close eye on me.”
“Mm... I'm listening. Could you tell me again before you continue? That way, at least I'll know how to get through it.”
“Thank you for telling me which step you're on. It's still frightening to hear, but it's better than being left to imagine things on my own.”
“Ah... Are you watching me because you're worried I won't be able to keep still? ...All right, then don't look away.”
“Doctor...? Why has everyone suddenly gone quiet? I understand you're concentrating, but at least tell me things are still going smoothly...”
“Is it really almost over? Thank goodness... I couldn't pretend I had everything under control this time. Thank you.”
“All right, slow breaths, just as you said... Hoo... I can do this. There's only a little left, right?”
“...You don't have to make me keep talking. Just call my name softly when it's all over... Thank you.”
“An enema is on the preparation list too? Sigh, even the toughest assignments never made me this embarrassed... Tell me how it works first.”
“I understand. It's part of preparing for surgery. I just never imagined this would be the hardest thing to talk about today...”
“Well, it seems the ward isn't a place where I get to negotiate. If it's necessary, I'll cooperate. Just please don't leave me flustered.”
“We don't need to do that? Phew, then I'll take back a little of that nervousness... Just a little.”
“Oh, an enema isn't part of today's preparation. Good. I can save my energy for the actual surgery.”
“Hair removal?... So you need to prepare that whole area. Yes, I know it's for the surgery, but it's still a little embarrassing.”
“Even safety checks in the cockpit don't scare me, yet lying here while a nurse removes hair feels so awkward... I never expected that.”
“All right, I won't move around. Please tell me which areas need to be exposed first, so I know what to expect.”
“No hair removal needed today... So not every preparation step has to be done every time.”
“We're skipping this step? Then I'll trust the professionals' judgment. Phew, I really am relieved.”
“Oh, my hair all goes into the cap like that? Looks like I won't be earning any style points today.”
“All right, surgical cap on. It really does feel a little like heading out on a mission... Except this time, I'm the one being given instructions.”
“All right, arms here, legs like this... Understood. I'm usually adjusting my own piloting position. Today, you're doing it for me.”
“This position is harder to hold than I expected. Yes, I'll cooperate. Just tell me before you adjust anything.”
“I'm still not used to being secured to the table... But if it keeps the procedure steady, I understand.”
“Wait, you're securing me like this without anesthesia? I know it's for safety, but I'm afraid I won't be able to stop myself from pulling away when it hurts!”
“Don't rush me into saying I'm fine... I don't even know how much it's going to hurt. I'm really starting to panic.”
“All right, I'll try to do as you say. But if I cry out, please don't think I'm joking...”
“I need a urinary catheter too... I understand it's part of the nursing care, but hearing that I'm going to have it done still makes me blush.”
“Nurse, please tell me when you're about to start. I'm usually good at joking around, but I can't manage a laugh right now.”
“All right, I'll cooperate. It's just... I feel really uncomfortable. Could I steady my breathing first?”
“No anesthesia, and I still need this preparation? I-I know it's necessary, but don't start without saying anything!”
“Wait... Once the catheter is in, you'll go straight to cutting? No, the more I think about it, the more frightened I get.”
“All right... I'll try to relax, but my body just won't listen. Please talk me through each step slowly.”
“Hss, that antiseptic is cold... I know it's normal preparation, but that really made it sink in that I'm about to have surgery.”
“Yes, go ahead. I'll lie still... Just don't suddenly go quiet. Give me a little warning so I can prepare myself.”
“This area is all disinfected... So cutting comes next? Wait, could you give me a little more time...”
“So cold... It's only disinfection, and I'm already stiff with nerves. Are we really starting without anesthesia?”
“I know I shouldn't move, but now every touch makes me think of that scalpel...”
“That's where you're going to cut, right... Seeing it drawn on with a pen makes it feel so real.”
“All right, I won't move. It's just that looking at that line suddenly gives me the creeps...”
“Wait, you've already marked the incision... Are you really going to cut along here without any anesthesia at all?”
“D-don't reach for the knife yet! I know the line is only a mark, but just seeing it is almost more than I can take...”
“I was just saying I wasn't scared... But as soon as you marked the spot, I suddenly couldn't bear to look.”
Doctor, I meant to finish my work before coming in, but my body suddenly started protesting: {line}
The most noticeable problem is this: {line}. I can explain what happened in order.
Yes, there's one more thing to add to the report: {line}. Oh, force of habit—don't mind me.
I'm Sagiri Sakurai, the chief of VTX Union's Special Operations Section 3 and the lead pilot of its test machine. I tend to make things sound lighthearted, but I don't take my work lightly.
strings.patient_bundles.patient_sagiri_sakurai.e: “I need to take off all my clothes for the examination? My, Doctor, your entry procedures are stricter than a cockpit's... Just kidding. Could you explain the scope of the examination first?”
“We're skipping this for now? Phew, that's a real relief. But don't leave anything that needs checking unresolved just because I was joking.”
“All right, understood. I'll cooperate. Just explain the scope of the examination first and give me a little time to prepare.”
“Thank you for explaining it so clearly. Then I'm in your hands... I may act carefree, but I really do get shy when it's my turn.”
“Hey, there's no need for that tone. I'll cooperate with a necessary examination, but the more you rush me, the harder it is to relax.”
strings.patient_bundles.patient_sagiri_sakurai.p: Sagiri Sakurai's Preoperative Arrangements
“Dr. Sakaguchi, today's the day I go into surgery, right? I've handed over my work. Is there anything else you need me to do here in the ward?”

“Could you explain it in a little more detail? Once I'm on the table, what order will everything happen in—from positioning and disinfection to the moment the blade actually comes down? ...I don't usually mind hearing the details, but this time I'm a little afraid I'll think about them too much.”

At first, Sagiri casually asks about the sequence of steps as though she were listening to a project briefing. The more carefully the staff explain the positioning, restraint, incision, and subsequent procedures, the harder it becomes for her to maintain her smile. She finally realizes that this time, she will not be facing risk from behind a control stick: her own body will undergo everything she has just heard.
You will be the lead surgeon for Sagiri Sakurai's operation. Confirm the responsibilities of the assistant surgeon, scrub nurse, and circulating nurse, and the staffing required for the current case.

Arrange Sagiri Sakurai's preoperative preparation according to the current case. Confirm the required nursing procedures and the nurses responsible; do not change the medical workflow based on her occupation.
“All the preparation is done? All right, the operating room is next... I can't distract myself with work talk anymore.”
You and the surgical team change, scrub, and complete the necessary sterile preparation before entering the operating room according to the established procedure.
“Wow, those lights are bright... Usually I'm the one in the pilot's seat, watching the screens. Having so many people gathered around me today feels completely different.”

The team checks Sagiri Sakurai's identity, current case, surgical plan, anesthesia status, and staff assignments one by one. She tries to respond in a lighthearted tone, but her clenched hands betray her nervousness.
Select and verify the procedure according to Sagiri Sakurai's current randomly assigned case and established treatment plan. Do not treat her occupational background as a fixed diagnosis.
“Wait, isn't that a different procedure from the one you mentioned earlier? Please check it first. I can't start up a machine with an inconsistent checklist either.”

Sagiri Sakurai has completed the preoperative preparation required for the current case and is positioned on the operating table. Confirm the anesthesia method, positioning, and conditions required to begin.
“Mm, I'm in your hands... I usually hate giving up control, but today I can only put my trust in all of you.”
Sagiri Sakurai is under general anesthesia and gives no conscious responses to the surgery. The team completes the final checks and begins according to the current procedure.
“My legs really are numb... My head is still awake, but I can't adjust my body myself. Doctor, please tell me before you start.”
“Has the local anesthetic taken effect? All right, I'll cooperate... But if something hurts wrong deeper inside, I'll definitely tell you.”
“Wait... Are we really starting just like this? I know I said I'd cooperate, but right now I don't feel ready at all!”
The lead surgeon requests the instruments required for the current procedure. The scrub nurse passes them over and confirms the operating conditions according to the established workflow.

The assistant surgeon confirms the exposure of the surgical field and the conditions for retraction, then waits for the lead surgeon's next instruction without changing the selected anesthesia pathway.

The team rechecks the planned incision and current anesthesia status. The scrub nurse places the required scalpel in the lead surgeon's hand, and the surgeon is about to begin along the planned incision.
Under general anesthesia, Sagiri Sakurai has no conscious patient dialogue. The team continues monitoring and proceeds with the planned operation.
During steps that require a patient response, the staff check Sagiri Sakurai's awareness and cooperation. If she is under general anesthesia, they continue monitoring and operating as required.

If Sagiri Sakurai remains conscious, she initially masks her nervousness with a lighthearted tone. As pain and her sense of lost control increase, her smile fades and she begins asking directly for help. If she is under general anesthesia, the staff continue monitoring and operating.
The operation enters its closing phase. If she is still conscious, use her corresponding closing responses; under general anesthesia, show only narration of the team's work and handover.
The team proceeds to the subsequent steps of the operation selected for the current case, with the assistant and nurses each carrying out their responsibilities.
The team completes the main part of the current procedure, checks the necessary subsequent steps, and continues according to the existing rules.
The operation is over. The team completes the necessary incision care, instrument count, documentation, and postoperative handover.
